newsitem.title: VANUATU: Vanuatu government toppled by no confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Vanuatu government toppled by no confidence vote.

text.p: The Vanuatu government was toppled on Monday when the South Pacific nation's parliament passed a vote of no confidence in Prime Minister Maxime Carlot.

Serge Vohor, leader of a faction of the ruling Union of Moderate Parties (UMP) and the only candidate standing against Carlot, was elected prime minister, heading a coalition of opposition parties, following a parliamentary vote.
The deputy prime ministership was expected to go to the opposition Melanesian Progressive Party's (MPP) Barak Sope.
Parliament voted 27 to 22 in favour of the vote of no confidence in Carlot, automatically toppling his government. The speaker is counted in the 50-seat parliament, but did not vote.
Leaving the parliament, Carlot said he believed his short seven months as prime minister had benefited Vanuatu.
"I am happy. I have nothing to regret. I am satisfied I did my best internally and internationally," Carlot told reporters.
The 80-island nation has been embroiled in a political crisis since the last election in November 1995 when no party won a majority in parliament.
The UMP, led by Vohor, formed a coalition in November. But in February 1996 Vohor resigned after dissident government members sought a no confidence vote against him.
Carlot then resigned as parliamentary speaker to become prime minister under a new coalition government, which included his former political rivals.
In turn, Vohor formed a breakaway opposition group and vowed to topple Carlot, but Carlot's new government still had a majority.
Three more government members defected to the opposition in a reshuffle in August, leaving the opposition with a 27-seat majority in parliament.
The government, facing a vote of no confidence, stalled by refusing to turn up to parliament.
But on Monday the Supreme Court of Vanuatu ruled an extraordinary session of parliament must sit to hear the vote of no confidence motion.
Vanuatu, formerly the New Hebrides, was governed jointly by Britain and France until independence in 1980.
